answer.rationale: The security patch cannot be rolled back (memory_b1 is therefore blocked). Write-path p99 is 5x target during peak settlement load, and customer writes must not be lost. memory_b3 demonstrates that adding capacity (headroom) absorbs write surges without disruption, but provisioning new capacity takes time we may not have at 90 minutes of degradation. memory_b2 shows regional failover restored latency fast, shifted traffic cleanly, and recovered error rates within minutes—exactly the speed and write-safety profile this situation demands. Failover redirects the write path to a healthy region, immediately relieving the saturated primary without reverting the security patch and without dropping in-flight writes (traffic shifts cleanly per the memory). route_read_replicas (memory_b5) would offload reads only, but the bottleneck here is on the write path, so it is insufficient. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) protects against a downstream dependency failure, but the symptom is latency climb, not a partner outage. add_capacity is the second-best option if failover is unavailable in the next window.
